caption:
Most of them in homes were stolen as chicks.

The scarlet macaw is one of the few birds whose color comes not just from pigment but from the structural geometry of its feathers, scattering red wavelengths the way the sky scatters blue, and a wild bird's plumage is brighter than anything a captive lineage will ever reach. Pairs mate for life and lay just one or two eggs per breeding cycle, in cavities high in old hardwoods, which makes the species exceptionally easy to poach. In Honduras and Guatemala, traffickers harvest entire clutches by climbing the nest trees during fledging week, and a chick that survives the journey to a US or European pet market is worth roughly two thousand dollars. The species lost an estimated forty percent of its Central American range in the last century to logging and the pet trade combined.
